title: Faith rises and falls
hookLine: many scholars teach that iman increases with good deeds and decreases with sins

lines: A WAY OF HOLDING THE SIX.
cards: Phone batteries have a little icon in the corner. Full, then less, then a red sliver, then you plug it in and watch it climb.
The six articles of faith could sound like a list you either have or don't, like a membership card. But the Qur'an and the hadith talk about iman more like that battery. It can be more.
It can be less. It can be topped up. Today closes the week, not with a seventh thing to believe, but with a way of holding the six.

teach.b: Back on day one hundred fifteen, a companion worried that his iman was low and heard: an hour, and an hour. Today, the teaching behind that. First, the verse.
The Qur'an speaks of Allah sending peace into the hearts of believers, in Pickthall's words, "that they might add faith unto their faith." Faith, in that verse, can grow.
Another verse says that when Allah's revelations are recited to believers, their faith increases. Second, the branches. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says iman has many branches.

teach.h: FROM THE TESTIMONY TO THE ROAD.
teach.b: The highest is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. The lowest is moving something harmful out of the road. And modesty, the hadith adds, is a branch too.
On this picture, faith reaches all the way down to a rock in the street.
Third, the scholars. Al-Bukhari titled a chapter on how faith increases and decreases, and a line of Sunni scholars teaches exactly that: good deeds raise it, sins lower it.

Hanafi and Maturidi scholars put it another way: the core of iman, the belief itself, doesn't grow or shrink, but its light and its fruits in a person's life do. Both views are held within Sunni Islam.
Last, why it matters. If faith can fall, a low day isn't the end of anything.

teach.h: ONE ROCK OUT OF THE ROAD.
teach.b: And if it can rise, the way back up is small and concrete: one branch, one deed, one rock moved out of the road.

how: In Muslim teaching, faith is spoken of as rising and falling, with good deeds, prayer and Qur'an recitation as ways to strengthen it; Hanafi and Maturidi scholars hold that the core of belief stays constant while its strength and fruits vary.

games.q: what does “faith rises and falls” mean?
o: faith can grow with good deeds and shrink with sins
faith is set at birth and stays the same for life
faith is strongest in Ramadan and fades the rest of the year

games.q: faith rises and falls — tap the pairs.
p: there is no god but Allah
moving harm out of the road
the core stays; its fruits vary

s: the Qur'an speaks of faith being added to faith
"that they might add faith unto their faith."
in the hadith, faith is only a belief in the head
its lowest branch is moving something harmful out of the road.
all Sunni scholars describe the rise and fall of faith the same way
Hanafi and Maturidi scholars say the core belief stays the same while its light and fruits vary.

games.q: what does the hadith in Sahih Muslim call the lowest branch of faith?
o: moving something harmful out of the road.
games.why: the highest branch is the testimony, and the lowest is moving harm out of the road. faith reaches all the way down to the street.

practice: Think of the lowest branch in the hadith, moving something harmful out of the way, and find where that is for you: a box blocking a hallway, a sharp comment you could leave out, a task left in someone's path.
Choose one, small and real, and picture yourself doing it start to finish. If you pray, you can ask that it be accepted; if not, simply decide.

wordCard.voice: Faith rises and falls. The teaching that iman can be added to by good deeds and lessened by sins; in the Qur'an's words, faith added to faith. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: faith grows. The six are done; tomorrow the theologians begin. See you then.
